pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that all rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() appends ' — priority' unless normal; 'AC-2' test asserts exact li text.
WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal with ordering.
Unfiltered query ORDER BY id; 'AC-4' test asserts the full list in order.
nav() renders the four filters with the current one as <strong>; 'AC-5' asserts exact nav HTML for all four views.
Returns 400 when the priority param is present and not in the set; 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__ values, and asserts no <li>.
Empty message is 'No X-priority items.' when the table is non-empty, else 'No items yet.'; 'AC-7' test covers both cases in every view.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; 'AC-8' test asserts it. The checker script and its test were updated to accept a query string.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and the owner's go. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-checker query-string allowance, which AC-8 needs and the PR discloses.
All 8 acceptance items are met and the decisions are followed. Every state-table row has a test in the 'states' describe block. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, with no later edits.

The tests assert exact rendered output and status codes, so they would fail if the code were wrong. I couldn't run them here because vitest isn't installed. The traffic fake app change loosens nothing.
The README describes the filter. CLAUDE.md and the README already say new routes go in routes.json, and that was done.
Input is validated against a whitelist. The 400 path runs before any query, and the SQL is parameterised. I found no defects.
Titles are still HTML-escaped. The priority value is whitelisted before it reaches the nav links or the empty message. The route regex relaxation still refuses spaces and '#'.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework, styling or stylesheet files in the diff, and no browser was available for visual review.
No UI flow could be demonstrated: there is no browser, and the PR gives no preview.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims about the migration, the tests, the traffic route and the checker change are all true of the diff.
